headline: PBOC Raises FX Reserve Requirement Ratio to Curb Yuan Rally and Ease Export Pressure
summary: The People's Bank of China raised the foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio to curb the yuan's sustained rally, providing relief to exporters amid a record goods trade surplus.
why: Central bank interventions in foreign exchange markets help manage currency appreciation velocity, protecting export competitiveness and trade balance stability.

impacts.name: Chinese Yuan
impacts.why: Raising reserve requirements directly targets and cools excessive currency appreciation.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The central bank intervened by raising foreign exchange reserve requirements to moderate the currency's rapid rise, easing appreciation pressures driven by massive trade surpluses.
